cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has another message from the LORD, and this one is about a land along the rivers of Cush. It opens with the one word you NEVER want at the top of a letter: "Woe." The land is called the land of whirring wings. Friend, I can HEAR that one.

cards.question: This land along the rivers of Cush sends out couriers. How do they travel?

cards.text: Then the call goes out for swift messengers to go. Swift. Not "whenever you get around to it." SWIFT. They're headed to a people who are tall and smooth-skinned, a powerful nation of strange speech.

cards.question: The swift messengers go to a nation described as a people nobody is afraid of.
What is the land of this tall, powerful nation like?

cards.text: Now Isaiah turns to everybody, all the people of the world and everyone living on the earth. Something is coming, and this is NOT a notification you can put on mute.

cards.question: Isaiah tells the whole world: when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will ___ it; when a ram's horn sounds, you will ___ it.

cards.text: Everybody's waiting on that banner and that horn. Then the prophet says, "For this is what the LORD has told me:"

cards.question: In Isaiah's message about Cush, what does the LORD say He will do from His dwelling place?
The LORD compares His watching to a crashing wave on the shore.

cards.text: Then the picture moves to a vineyard. It's before the harvest, the blossom is gone, and the flower is turning into a ripening grape. And He doesn't wait around.

cards.question: Before the harvest in Isaiah's vineyard picture, what does He do to the shoots?

answers.text: Cuts them off with a pruning knife
Waters them with the morning dew
Ties them up to a wooden stake

cards.question: After cutting off the shoots, He keeps the branches safe for later.

cards.text: Those cut branches don't get cleaned up. Nobody's coming with a broom. They sit out there from summer all the way to winter.

cards.question: In Isaiah's vineyard picture, the cut branches are left for the birds of prey and the wild animals.

cards.text: Then the last verse flips EVERYTHING. That tall, smooth-skinned, widely feared nation from the start shows up again, and this time they're coming to the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: What does the tall, widely feared nation from the land divided by rivers bring to the LORD of Hosts?
The gifts are brought to Mount ___, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Isaiah the prophet has another message...', 'It opens with...', 'The land is called...' and 'Friend, I can HEAR that one.' The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The story card has 5 sentences: 'Then the call goes out...', 'Swift.', 'Not "whenever you get around to it."', 'SWIFT.' and 'They're headed to...'. The limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Everybody's waiting on that banner and that horn' adds a fact that is not in the text. Isaiah 18:3 says that when the banner is raised and the horn sounds, people will see and hear them. It never says anyone is waiting.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The LORD's two comparisons in Isaiah 18:4, shimmering heat in the sunshine and a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest, never appear on any card. The only card about them is a false statement about a crashing wave. The baker leaves without ever learning the passage's actual picture.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Then the picture moves to a vineyard.', 'It's before the harvest...' and 'And He doesn't wait around.' The limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Those cut branches don't get cleaned up.', 'Nobody's coming with a broom.' and 'They sit out there from summer all the way to winter.' The limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'The last verse flips EVERYTHING' and 'this time they're coming to the LORD of Hosts' add two things the text doesn't say. They frame verse 7 as a reversal of what came before, and they say the nation itself comes. Isaiah 18:7 only says 'At that time' gifts will be brought from this people to Mount Zion. It leaves open how verse 7 connects to verses 5 and 6, and who carries the gifts.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
